title: HeimUI Screen
description: Wire contract for a HeimUI server-driven screen. Any backend, in any language, that emits JSON matching this document can drive a HeimUI client. Field names are snake_case; every component is discriminated by its `type`.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, so editors can offer completion. Ignored by the client.

id.description: Identifier of this screen. Independent from the id used to request it.

version.description: Screen version. Form drafts saved against a different version are discarded rather than restored onto changed fields.

apply_safe_insets.description: Whether the client pads the screen for system bars and notches.

metadata.description: Free-form data passed through to the host app untouched.

signature.description: Deprecated in the body. Send the signature in the X-Heim-Signature header so it can cover the exact response bytes.

component.description: A component is discriminated by `type`. Known types are validated strictly. An UNKNOWN type is accepted on purpose: forward compatibility is a core property of the system — a newer server ships a component and older clients render a fallback while the rest of the tree survives. The trade-off is that a typo like "contaner" passes validation here and shows as a fallback on the device.

id.description: Unique within its sibling list. Duplicates are disambiguated by the client, but relying on that is a bug: the id is also the test tag and the list key.

visible_if.description: Client-side visibility expression: "is_admin", "plan == 'PREMIUM'", "age >= 18", "!hidden". Evaluated against form state. An unresolved key evaluates to false. NOT an authorization mechanism: the payload already reached the device.

padding.description: Applied to the container's own box, inside the scroll viewport — the padding scrolls away with the content. For a chip strip or carousel that must keep a fixed inset while scrolling edge to edge, use lazy_row instead, where padding becomes scroll-safe content padding.

spacing.description: Gap between children in dp. With a SPACE_* arrangement this is the minimum gap, not the exact one.

scrollable.description: Scrolls along `direction`. Set false when nesting inside another scroller on the same axis.

arrangement.description: How children are distributed along the container's own axis. Distinct from `alignment`, which positions them across the other axis: in a VERTICAL container `alignment` decides left/centre/right and `arrangement` decides top/centre/spread. PACKED is the default and separates children by `spacing`. The distributing values (SPACE_*) treat `spacing` as a minimum gap rather than replacing it.

weight.description: Share of the parent container's main axis. Two children with weight 1 split a row in half; 2 and 1 split it two thirds to one third. Any component may carry it. Ignored unless the parent is a `container`, and ignored inside a scrolling container — a scrolling axis is unbounded, so there is nothing to divide.

action.description: Discriminated by `type`. Known actions are validated strictly; an unknown action is accepted and degrades on the client without taking down the screen that declares it.

validation_rule.description: Rules run as the user types AND again before submission, so a field the user never touched still blocks an invalid form.

value.description: REGEX: the pattern (max 256 chars). MIN_LENGTH/MAX_LENGTH: the bound. CUSTOM: the validator name. A CUSTOM name the host has not registered FAILS the field — it is never skipped.

color.description: A Material 3 token name, a brand token registered by the host, or a hex value (#RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB). Unrecognised values fall back to the component's default.

typography.description: A Material 3 type-scale token, or a brand text style the host registered via HeimBrandTokens. Deliberately not a closed enum: brand tokens exist so a payload can name a treatment the design team owns ("price", "legal"), and a schema that rejected those would defeat them. An unrecognised name falls back to bodyMedium.

padding.description: Padding in dp. A number applies to all four sides; an object sets sides independently. Use start/end rather than left/right so the same payload mirrors correctly in right-to-left locales. An explicit side overrides the shorthand that would otherwise set it, whatever order the keys appear in.

anyOf.description: The same padding on all four sides.

all.description: All four sides. Overridden by any narrower key.

start.description: Leading edge: left in LTR, right in RTL.

end.description: Trailing edge: right in LTR, left in RTL.

frame.description: Intrinsic dimensions, in dp. Reach for min_height/min_width first: they guarantee a floor while letting the component grow, so a card stays consistent in a list without breaking when the content is longer than the author expected. Use aspect_ratio for anything whose proportion matters more than its measurement. Fixed width/height do NOT grow — right for an avatar or an icon frame, wrong for anything containing text, because a user running their font at 200% for accessibility will see it clipped and cannot do anything about it. A fixed dimension overrides the minimum on the same axis; aspect_ratio applies only when exactly one axis is otherwise constrained.

min_height.description: Floor in dp. The component still grows past it when its content needs to. Prefer this to height.

min_width.description: Floor in dp. Prefer this to width.

aspect_ratio.description: width / height, e.g. 1.78 for 16:9. Applied when exactly one axis is otherwise constrained.

height.description: Fixed dp. Does not grow with the user's font scale — do not put text in it.

width.description: Fixed dp. Does not grow with the user's font scale — do not put text in it.

action_set_state.description: Writes a value into the screen's form state. Purely local — nothing leaves the device. This is what lets anything that is not an input drive visible_if: selecting a card, switching a tab, expanding a section. Combine it with another action when the change must also reach the server; actions run in the order the list declares them.

key.description: State key to write, the same namespace text_field and switch use.

value.description: Any JSON value. Null writes an empty string rather than removing the key, because visible_if distinguishes empty from never-set.

tracking.description: Business analytics to report when this action runs. Opaque to the SDK: it carries the names your analytics team chose and hands the map to the app's HeimTrackingDispatcher, which decides where they go. The point is that renaming an event becomes a backend deploy instead of an app release.

checkbox.description: A single yes/no bound to state. Prefer it over `switch` when the meaning is agreement rather than a setting — 'I accept the terms' is a checkbox, 'dark mode' is a switch. The whole row is the tap target, not just the box.

weight.description: Share of the parent container's main axis. Two children with weight 1 split a row in half; 2 and 1 split it two thirds to one third. Any component may carry it. Ignored unless the parent is a `container`, and ignored inside a scrolling container — a scrolling axis is unbounded, so there is nothing to divide.

radio_group.description: One choice from a list, all visible at once. Right up to about five options; past that use `select`, because a long radio list pushes everything else off the screen.

weight.description: Share of the parent container's main axis. Two children with weight 1 split a row in half; 2 and 1 split it two thirds to one third. Any component may carry it. Ignored unless the parent is a `container`, and ignored inside a scrolling container — a scrolling axis is unbounded, so there is nothing to divide.

options.description: Choices. `value` is stored and submitted; `label` is read. An option with a blank value is dropped, because it could never be stored.

select.description: One choice, revealed on demand. The shape for a country or document-type list. The field shows the option's label while state holds its value, so labels can be translated without the stored value moving.

weight.description: Share of the parent container's main axis. Two children with weight 1 split a row in half; 2 and 1 split it two thirds to one third. Any component may carry it. Ignored unless the parent is a `container`, and ignored inside a scrolling container — a scrolling axis is unbounded, so there is nothing to divide.

options.description: Choices. `value` is stored and submitted; `label` is read. An option with a blank value is dropped, because it could never be stored.

date_picker.description: Date input. State always holds ISO-8601 YYYY-MM-DD, never the localised text the user saw: the value travels to a backend, and 15/03/2024 is 15 March in Bogota and unparseable where the month comes first. Bounds are compared in UTC, because a calendar date has no time zone and treating it as an instant moves a birth date by a day west of Greenwich.

weight.description: Share of the parent container's main axis. Two children with weight 1 split a row in half; 2 and 1 split it two thirds to one third. Any component may carry it. Ignored unless the parent is a `container`, and ignored inside a scrolling container — a scrolling axis is unbounded, so there is nothing to divide.

chip.description: A compact tappable label — a category pill, a tag, a filter. Fills the gap between `badge`, which is decoration and cannot be tapped, and `button`, which is the wrong shape for a strip of them. Put a row of them in a `lazy_row` so they scroll edge to edge while keeping their inset.

weight.description: Share of the parent container's main axis. Two children with weight 1 split a row in half; 2 and 1 split it two thirds to one third. Any component may carry it. Ignored unless the parent is a `container`, and ignored inside a scrolling container — a scrolling axis is unbounded, so there is nothing to divide.

icon.description: Icon name, resolved by the app's HeimIconProvider.

variant.description: FILTER announces itself as selected or not to a screen reader; ASSIST announces an action. Using one for the other is the difference between hearing 'selected' and hearing nothing.

state_key.description: Binds the chip to form state. With `value`, chips sharing a key behave as one choice and tapping the selected one clears it. Without `value`, the chip is an independent on/off for a multi-select row. Omit both for a plain action chip.

value.description: This chip's value within its group. Requires `state_key`.

rich_text.description: Text made of styled runs, so one paragraph can mix weights, colours and links. This is the component for 'I accept the [terms and conditions]' with only the bracketed part linked — splitting that into three components puts a line break where the sentence should flow. There is no HTML: a fixed set of span properties, because handing a payload a markup renderer is handing it a capability you cannot take back.

weight.description: Share of the parent container's main axis. Two children with weight 1 split a row in half; 2 and 1 split it two thirds to one third. Any component may carry it. Ignored unless the parent is a `container`, and ignored inside a scrolling container — a scrolling axis is unbounded, so there is nothing to divide.

spans.description: Runs, rendered in order as one paragraph.

style.description: Overrides the paragraph style for this run.

color.description: Design token or #RRGGBB. Ignored on a linked run, which uses the theme's link colour.

weight.description: thin | light | normal | medium | semibold | bold | black, or 100-900.

url.description: Makes the run a link. Opened through the same HeimUrlLauncher and scheme policy as `open_url` — a link inside a paragraph is not a way around the allow-list.

style.description: Base style every span inherits unless it overrides it.
